scope.description: Five real OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5) in one process, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1. Node 1 leads and decides entries 1..4 everywhere; entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by 1 after 1,2,3,5 accept, but the Decide reaches only node 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only, and node 5's delayed Prepare makes it promise in Accept phase. Node 5's decided index and the status of the entry at index 4 are sampled before, immediately after the AcceptSync, and after the new leader re-decides.
assumptions: Messages are delivered synchronously to their addressed node when routed; omitted messages are dropped, which the library's own resend and prepare-request paths are designed to repair.
Holding one Accepted(5) reply from nodes 3 and 4 while node 5 promises models slow acknowledgement, not a Byzantine or corrupted message.
No ticks are called, so leadership is obtained only through try_become_leader and BLE elections do not occur.

basis.prefix: Build nodes 1..5 from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]} with MemoryStorage and settle. node1.try_become_leader(); settle so all five promise. Deliver the held Prepare to node 5, settle so its late Promise reaches node 2 and node 2 answers with AcceptSync carrying its decided index. Emit late_sync phase=after_sync (decided, decided_before, entry status, leader2 decided, regressed). Then deliver the held Accepted(5) replies, settle, and emit late_sync phase=after_redecide.

comparisons.description: After the AcceptSync, node 5's decided index is lower than before and the same index reads as undecided.
After the new leader re-decides, node 5 is back at decided 5, so the same entry was observed decided, undecided and decided again.

scope.description: Five OmniPaxos instances. Node 1 is made leader, appends entries 1 and 2 with full delivery, then reconfigures, so every node accepts entries 1..2 and the StopSign. Node 5 is then moved to the Prepare phase under ballot 2 and receives a crafted AcceptSync whose log_sync has sync_idx 3, an empty suffix and the StopSign, a prefix that already covers the position where node 5 holds the StopSign.
assumptions: Moving node 5 to Prepare with a higher ballot and then delivering an AcceptSync with that ballot is the same state transition a leader would drive.
The payload deliberately covers the StopSign position and also carries the StopSign, modelling the sync a follower can receive after it already accepted the marker.
No snapshots or trimming are involved, so accepted and decided indices are directly comparable.
excluded: Randomized loss, leadership churn, the next configuration being started, snapshots and flexible quorums.

scope.description: One OmniPaxos instance is built over a MemoryStorage that holds exactly the fields the covering-sync witness leaves behind: two appended entries, the StopSign for configuration 2, and decided index 4. The test emits the stored fields, builds the node with pid 5, and emits accepted, decided, is_reconfigured, the entry kinds at indices 2 and 3, and whether the decided suffix from index 0 is readable.
assumptions: The covering-sync witness writes two entries and the StopSign and persists decided 4 through update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx; its accepted index of 4 exists only in the cache, so these storage fields are the state a restart would load.
OmniPaxos exposes no accessor for a live node's storage in this snapshot, so the probe reconstructs those persisted fields directly instead of dumping them from the witness node.
A reload with decided above the recomputed accepted index is the situation a client would meet after that node restarts.
excluded: The write path that produced the fields, snapshots, trimming, the next configuration being started, and any message exchange after the restart.

basis.prefix: The test restart_after_covering_sync_cannot_read_decided_log builds a MemoryStorage, appends Value(1) and Value(2), stores StopSign::with(configuration_id 2, nodes 1..5, no metadata) and sets the decided index to 4, then emits stored with the log length, the decided index and the StopSign flag. It builds OmniPaxos for pid 5 in configuration 1 over that storage and emits restart with accepted, decided, is_reconfigured, entry_status(read(2)), entry_status(read(3)), whether read_decided_suffix(0) is None and the returned length.

comparisons.description: The reload recomputes accepts 3 from the two stored entries plus the marker, one lower than the inflated accepted index of 4 the node reported before the restart, while the decided index stays 4.
With decided 4 above the recomputed accepted 3, read_decided_suffix(0) finds the range end beyond the accepted index and returns None, so the decided log cannot be read after the restart.

scope.description: One OmniPaxos instance is built over a MemoryStorage holding two entries, the StopSign for configuration 2, decided index 4 and the promise ballot carried by the covering witness's Prepare. The test emits the stored fields, builds pid 5 in configuration 1, drains the messages construction queued, and emits accepted, decided, is_reconfigured, the entry kinds at indices 2 and 3, whether the decided suffix from index 0 is None, its length and the number of queued PrepareReq messages.
assumptions: The covering witness persists decided 4 and the promise it gave, so these storage fields are what a restart would load.
Load recomputes the accepted index and reads the same fields whether or not a promise is stored, so the unreadable suffix should be unchanged by adding it.
A stored promise makes construction queue one PrepareReq per configured peer, which is four for pid 5 in a five-node configuration.
excluded: The write path that produced the fields, snapshots, trimming, delivery of the queued PrepareReq messages and any response to them.

basis.prefix: The test restart_after_covering_sync_cannot_read_decided_log builds a MemoryStorage, appends Value(1) and Value(2), stores StopSign::with(configuration_id 2, nodes 1..5, no metadata), sets decided to 4 and stores Ballot {config_id 1, n 2, priority 0, pid 9}, then emits stored. It builds OmniPaxos for pid 5 in configuration 1, drains the outgoing messages and emits restart with accepted, decided, is_reconfigured, entry_status(read(2)), entry_status(read(3)), suffix_none as a boolean, suffix_len and the count of queued PrepareReq messages.

comparisons.description: The reload recomputes accepted 3 from the two stored entries plus the marker while decided stays 4, even with the promise present.
With decided 4 above the recomputed accepted 3, read_decided_suffix(0) returns None; the flag is now a JSON boolean so the assertion matches its type.
Because the promise is stored, construction starts the node in Recover and queues one PrepareReq to each of the four peers, which is the recovery start the earlier limitation described.
